findings.claim: Removing the `addDirtyMock` bound alias will break any remaining reference to it, and any place where it was passed as a detached callback must now pass a properly bound function.
findings.rationale: `addDirtyMock` was a `.bind`-ed alias precisely because `Set.prototype.add` throws `TypeError: Method Set.prototype.add called on incompatible receiver undefined` when invoked without its receiver. If the rest of the file (not shown in this hunk) still references `addDirtyMock`, this is a compile error; if callers were converted to something like `onDirty: DIRTY_MOCK_STATES.add` (unbound) rather than `mock => DIRTY_MOCK_STATES.add(mock)`, it becomes a runtime TypeError on the first dirty-state notification. I can't see the call sites in this hunk, so confidence is moderate — worth verifying every former usage was rewritten to a bound/arrow form.

findings.claim: If the removal also dropped the only writer to `DIRTY_MOCK_STATES`, the set becomes dead code while still being a strong-reference container.
findings.rationale: The surrounding design deliberately uses `WeakRef`/`FinalizationRegistry` for `REGISTERED_MOCKS` to avoid retaining mocks, but `DIRTY_MOCK_STATES` is a plain `Set` holding strong references. After removing the convenience adder, please confirm the set is still populated and, more importantly, still cleared; otherwise it is either unused dead state or a place where mocks are retained for the lifetime of the module. Low-to-moderate confidence since the mutation sites aren't in this hunk.
